A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same optimization benchmark and ReSocratic synthesis work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; E-OPT is renamed OPTIBENCH, and relocated content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, synthetic-data accuracy measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Self-Instruct results in Table 4 and NL4OPT-E evaluations in Appendix A, Table 5.

M1.justification: The seed-based, stepwise synthesis, rule and similarity filters, code verification, and question/code translation procedures are retained. v2's three-stage exposition and explicit execution/rejection pathway in Figure 3 clarify procedures already described in v1 Section 4. The appendix prompts are substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix A adds evaluation on NL4OPT-E, an end-to-end adaptation of NL4OPT's linear, non-tabular problems; v1 discussed NL4OPT only as prior work. The renamed 605-question benchmark and ReSocratic-29k retain their stated linear/nonlinear and tabular/non-tabular coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Self-Instruct to the synthesis-method comparison. The existing WizardLM/Wizard comparator is relabeled Evol-Instruct with matching results, rather than replaced. The main LLM comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds the NL4OPT conversion and zero-shot cross-benchmark comparison, while removing the mean-cosine alignment measurement from v1 Appendix B.2.2. Annotation reporting shifts from consensus-based retention/discarding to additional review and correction; this does not establish that the dataset was rebuilt. Existing evaluation prompts, answer-accuracy criterion, and SFT budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the zero-shot difficulty breakdowns in v1 Figure 7 and the quantitative train-test alignment diagnostic in Figure 10. The few-shot breakdowns move from v1 Figure 8 to v2 Figure 6 and gain averages and trend lines. The filter/step-question ablations and t-SNE visualization remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6(b) adds linear trend-line estimates to the accuracy-by-variable-count analysis; v1 Figure 8(b) showed bars without those estimates. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, random-seed results, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched scores in Tables 2-3 remain unchanged. Table 4 adds Self-Instruct's 80.0% data accuracy and 10.7% overall accuracy; Table 5 adds NL4OPT-E accuracies of 89.3%, 83.0%, and 93.1% for DeepSeek-V2, GPT-3.5-Turbo, and GPT-4. Distribution statistics also change beyond rounding: synthetic samples with at most two variables rise from 6.4% calculated from v1's counts to 17.9% in v2 Figure 4. Removed diagnostic scores disappear. The PDFs do not establish an underlying dataset revision.

T1.justification: The optimization formulations and end-to-end evaluation equations are retained, and neither version develops theorems or proofs. The removed mean-cosine expression documents the discarded empirical diagnostic rather than a distinct theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a benchmark covering nonlinear and tabular optimization, a reverse Socratic synthesis method, and improved small-model performance through ReSocratic-29k fine-tuning. The renamed benchmark and shortened abstract do not materially change these contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's explanation of anomalous nonlinear-table SFT performance through train-test mismatch and its specific limitation concerning insufficiently diverse seed scenarios. It emphasizes dataset diversity, adds an intermediate-reasoning explanation for reverse synthesis, and interprets NL4OPT-E results as showing that benchmark is comparatively easy. Most performance interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies the SFT system/user/assistant template. It removes the dataset datasheets and licensing/maintenance disclosures, including annotator-background information, and omits the BERT model and pooling details used for the retained t-SNE visualization. Core prompts, synthesis settings, hardware, and training hyperparameters remain. The repository disclosure moves to the abstract; it is not a newly announced release.

R1.justification: v2 removes the generic LLM survey and associated citations, adds formal-reasoning work such as TRIGO, MUSTARD, and Lean 4 autoformalization, and revises its characterization of ORLM. Appendix A expands positioning against NL4OPT and implicit-number benchmarks. These are focused revisions within the retained optimization-modeling and reverse-synthesis positioning.

P1.justification: The title, benchmark terminology, and scenario/demonstration terminology change throughout. The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition receive substantial editing. Dataset statistics and selected analyses move into expanded experimental subsections, while the appendix contents page, datasheets, and limitations sections disappear. This substantially reorganizes the narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 are substantially redrawn, including a clearer evaluation workflow. Separate dataset-statistics figures become combined percentage plots, and t-SNE panels are rearranged and relocated. Tables reorder columns and rows; Table 1 adds dataset sizes and drops its MAMO row. v2 also adds Table 5 and the implicit/explicit example figure, while removing two diagnostic figures.

improvement.justification: The additional NL4OPT-E and Self-Instruct comparisons and clearer workflow figures are useful. However, the main accuracy evidence is unchanged, while v2 removes the specific distribution-mismatch analysis and limitation, along with provenance and licensing documentation. It also introduces unexplained distribution changes: Figure 4's synthetic question-length percentages total 98.3%, whereas v1's corresponding counts reconcile with its dataset total. These losses in transparency and numerical consistency outweigh the limited evidential and presentation gains.
